class.name: NetwClock
class.brief_description: The tick every peer in the session counts, reached by [member NetwSession.clock].
class.description:
A tick is a numbered step of the simulation. Every peer counts the same ticks, and a client keeps its count in step with the server's. [member tick] is the number every [NetwRecord] and lag compensation uses. [codeblock] @onready var clock: NetwClock = Netw.session(self).clock
func _ready() -> void: clock.before_tick.connect(sample_input) clock.ticked.connect(show_tick) [/codeblock] [b]How a tick is produced[/b] Each physics frame adds its delta to an accumulator, and every [code]1 / tickrate[/code] seconds in it runs one tick. A slow frame can run two ticks and a fast one none. At a [member tickrate] of 30 with 60 physics ticks per second, a tick runs every second frame, and [member physics_factor] is [code]2.0[/code]. At most [constant NetwMultiplayer.CLOCK_PARAM_MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME] ticks run in one frame. [member behind_count] counts how often that limit was hit. [b]How a client follows the server[/b] The client pings the server every [member ping_interval] seconds. The server answers with its tick, and the client aims ahead of it by half the round trip plus [constant NetwMultiplayer.CLOCK_PARAM_LEAD_TICKS]. The first answer sets the tick directly. After that, [member sync_mode] decides. [constant SYNC_MODE_SNAP] sets the tick directly every time, which can move it backwards. [constant SYNC_MODE_STRETCH], the default, runs the clock slightly faster or slower each frame by [constant NetwMultiplayer.CLOCK_PARAM_STRETCH_NUDGE_FACTOR] of the difference, so the tick never jumps. A difference larger than [constant NetwMultiplayer.CLOCK_PARAM_PANIC_SNAP_THRESHOLD] ticks is snapped. [b]Showing remote state[/b] State from other peers arrives late, so remote entities are shown [member display_offset] ticks in the past. [member recommended_display_offset] is the offset the current connection needs, the one-way latency plus the jitter times [constant NetwMultiplayer.CLOCK_PARAM_JITTER_MULTIPLIER], in ticks. It is not applied automatically. [method NetwMultiplayer.clock_auto_configure_offset] applies it.

method.name: monitor
method.description: Returns one clock diagnostic value. [codeblock] var rtt := clock.monitor(NetwClock.CLOCK_MONITOR_RTT_AVG) [/codeblock]

members.member: How many frames could not run every tick they needed. If it keeps growing, this machine is too slow for [member tickrate].
How many ticks in the past remote entities are shown. See [member recommended_display_offset].
[code]true[/code] once the settings from [method Netw.configure_clock] are applied. [member tick] does not move before that.
[code]true[/code] once the tick follows the server. Always [code]true[/code] on the server.
Physics frames per tick. Multiply a per-frame value by it to get a per-tick value.
Seconds between pings. Shorter follows the connection more closely and sends more packets.
The [member display_offset] the current connection needs, in ticks.
How the tick is corrected toward the server's.
How far time has moved past the last tick, in ticks, and it can exceed 1. Use it to interpolate.
How far into the current tick the clock is, from [code]0.0[/code] to [code]1.0[/code].
Ticks per second, set by [method Netw.configure_clock]. The same on every peer.

signal.name: before_tick
signal.description: Emitted before [param tick] runs. Read input here.

signal.name: ticked
signal.description: Emitted after every entity ran [code]_network_tick[/code] for [param tick]. Read results here.

Push a warning and continue. The default.
Notify [constant NetwMultiplayer.CLOCK_TICKRATE_MISMATCH] and let the game decide.
The most recent round-trip time, in seconds.
The round-trip time averaged over [constant NetwMultiplayer.CLOCK_PARAM_JITTER_WINDOW] samples, in seconds.
Seconds per tick, one divided by [constant NetwMultiplayer.CLOCK_PARAM_TICKRATE].
Seconds collected toward the next tick.
Physics frames run since the clock started.
[method MultiplayerAPI.poll] calls since the clock started.
Real seconds since the clock started.
